_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Burkina Faso researched as part of a second WAEMU/CEMAC push (following G.11's Senegal/Côte d'Ivoire/Mali/Cameroon batch). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: The high-value target this session -- has any WAEMU country's own statistics office named the base-2023 UEMOA regulation by number -- came up NOT FOUND for Burkina Faso specifically: three separate INSD monthly notes (April 2025, July 2025, February 2026), all checked directly, carry identical boilerplate that never cites a regulation number or the 20 December 2024 Bamako Council of Ministers session. The underlying institutional fact was independently confirmed via BCEAO's own communiqué instead (see uemoa-reg-2024-base2023, minted in this session's Togo slice, which independently located and OCR'd the regulation's actual gazette text). Burkina Faso's own IMF e-GDDS metadata, though stale (dated 2018), does name AFRISTAT directly as a co-producer of the reference WAEMU methodology guide -- a second country (after Senegal) to do so in this branch.

_open_questions.question: Burkina Faso's own 2018 IMF metadata names a document titled 'Harmonized Consumer Price Index of WAEMU Member Countries -- Theory and Practice' (WAEMU Commission, 1991, produced with AFRISTAT/EU/Eurocost/Eurostat/BCEAO assistance) as the reference methodology brochure. This is the same title Senegal's own SDDS metadata named last session (G.11) -- still not located as a retrievable document by either country's research pass.

No CARFO (civil-service) pension revaluation announcement newer than October 2020 was located, and no CNSS (private-sector) revaluation newer than a 2020 secondary-source article. Given Burkina Faso's 2022 coup and ongoing insurgency-driven instability, this gap is worth checking directly rather than assuming either continuity or suspension.

Loi n°004-2021/AN du 6 avril 2021 (CNSS's governing social-security law) is hosted as an image-only scanned PDF with no extractable text layer -- any indexation article it may contain could not be checked this session.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique et de la Démographie (INSD)
reports.description:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18, round 15/Wave C): Independently re-checked INSD's own live methodology voice on two current sources (the February 2026 base-2023 monthly note and the insd.bf/fr/indice page). Both reconfirm UEMOA/WAEMU harmonization in INSD's own words but continue to NOT name COICOP, the IMF/ILO CPI Manual, or AFRISTAT in descriptive prose — full-text search of the February 2026 note returned zero matches for "COICOP", "AFRISTAT", "FMI", "IMF", "OIT", or "ILO". On insd.bf/fr/indice, "AFRISTAT" appears only as a footer partner-link icon (alongside "Ministère des finances PNIN CNS AFRISTAT"), not as an attributive methodology sentence — do not treat that footer link as INSD naming AFRISTAT methodologically. This sharpens (does not contradict) the existing 'lineage, not current proof' caveat on this node's dependency to afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 below.

Burkina Faso's official harmonised consumer price index, base 2023 (replacing base 2014, itself replacing base 2008). "L'Institut National de la Statistique et de la Démographie (INSD) a le plaisir de mettre à la disposition des utilisateurs l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC) base 2023 en remplacement de l'indice base 2014... La période de base de l'IHPC est l'année 2023 et les pondérations de l'indice proviennent d'une enquête sur les dépenses des ménages réalisée en 2021." Covers all 13 administrative regions (a documented expansion from Ouagadougou-only pre-October 2018, to 5 regions, to 13 regions at base 2023), ~838 products, 3,951 observation points, ~25,000 monthly price collections. Formula per INSD's own 2018 IMF metadata (describing the then-current base-1996 index, not re-confirmed for the current base): Standard Laspeyres Aggregation.
reports.cadence_note: Per INSD's own 2018 IMF metadata: published by the 10th of month m+1. Corroborated by monthly note dates (April 2025, July 2025, February 2026 editions all directly retrieved this session).

reports.title: Guide Méthodologique de l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation dans la Zone UEMOA
reports.description: AFRISTAT's technical methodological guide for the base-2014 generation of the UEMOA-wide harmonised CPI (PDF creation date 2014-04-16), produced as executing technical body for the UEMOA Commission's IHPC renovation project: "En confiant à AFRISTAT l'exécution du projet de rénovation de l'Indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation dans ses pays membres, la Commission de l'UEMOA témoigne une fois de plus de l'excellence des relations qui existent entre ces deux institutions." Defines the NCOA-IHPC classification as directly derived from COICOP. A one-off foundational instrument for the base-2014 generation, since superseded at country level by base-2023 rebasings.

reports.title: Social Safety Net Project (P124015)
reports.description: World Bank cash-transfer and adaptive-safety-net project for Burkina Faso, approved 23 April 2014, revised closing date 31 March 2024. "The PDO is to increase access of poor and vulnerable households to safety nets and to lay the foundations for an adaptive safety net system in Burkina Faso." Delivered a flat, non-CPI-indexed transfer: "households are receiving 35,000 CFA per quarter over a period of three years." This Implementation Status & Results Report was archived 22 December 2022; status after the March 2024 closing date not checked this session.

dependencies.basis: AFRISTAT's guide states the NCOA-IHPC classification (used to structure INSD's own IHPC tables, e.g. 'Tableau 5: Évolution des indices nationaux suivant les groupes de la NCOA-IHPC') 'est directement dérivée de la nomenclature internationale COICOP', and was produced as the UEMOA-wide harmonised methodology INSD's own note describes ('le même instrument de suivi de l'évolution des prix a été mis en place dans les pays membres de l'UEMOA'). This specific guide covers the base-2014 generation; the equivalent base-2023 guide (annexed to uemoa-reg-2024-base2023, minted this session via the Togo slice) was not independently re-confirmed as INSD's current methodology source -- treat this edge as evidencing the lineage, not proof of current dependency.

Burkina Faso's own IMF DSBB metadata page for the CPI category is explicitly headed "Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (As provided by Burkina Faso as a participant in the e-GDDS)" -- reusing the imf-e-gdds node already minted for Kenya/Ethiopia/Ghana/Nigeria in this branch. Burkina Faso is confirmed on the e-GDDS (not SDDS) tier; dsbb.imf.org rendered fully via a live browser session this time.

_dropped.edge: bf-insd-ihpc's own documents -> UEMOA Council of Ministers regulation (base-2023 adoption)
_dropped.why: Three consecutive INSD monthly notes (April 2025, July 2025, February 2026) were checked directly and all carry byte-for-byte identical boilerplate that never cites a regulation number or the 20 December 2024 Bamako Council of Ministers session. The adoption itself is now confirmed via a different WAEMU institution's document (BCEAO's own communiqué, and -- independently and more completely -- the UEMOA Bulletin Officiel itself, located and OCR'd this session via the Togo research pass; see uemoa-reg-2024-base2023). Burkina Faso's own INSD simply never names it.

A 2020 government announcement of a CARFO pension revaluation (2.5% for categories A/B/P/military officers, 5% for other pensioners) is explicitly a discretionary Conseil des ministres decision motivated by general 'évolution du coût de la vie' language and political pressure, not a stated CPI figure or formula: 'Le gouvernement vient donc d'accéder à la requête.' CARFO's own initial-award formula (final salary x 2% x years of service) is separately wage-based with no revaluation clause on CARFO's own site. No revaluation newer than 2020 was located despite searching (see bf-carfo-cnss-2023-2026-revaluation-gap).

A 2020 press article (not CNSS's own official text) describes the CNSS pension floor as tied to the SMIG (minimum wage) at 84%, not to CPI: 'la pension ne doit pas être inférieure à 84% du SMIG.' The underlying law (Loi n°004-2021/AN) could not be independently checked -- its PDF is an unreadable image-only scan (see bf-cnss-law-2021-unreadable).

_dropped.edge: 'Harmonized Consumer Price Index of WAEMU Member Countries – Theory and Practice' (1991, WAEMU Commission) -> (not minted)

This is the same document title Senegal's own SDDS metadata named in G.11 -- now independently confirmed to exist and be named by a second WAEMU country's own IMF metadata submission, still not locatable as a retrievable file.

The project's own Implementation Status & Results Report describes a flat transfer amount ('35,000 CFA per quarter over a period of three years') with no CPI, inflation, or indexation language anywhere in the retrieved text.
